input:
Three critics review a book. For the three critics the odds in favor of the book are 2:5, 3:4 and 4:3 respectively. The probability that the majority is in favor of the book, is given by

Options:
A. 183/343
B. 160/343
C. 209/343
D. 134/343

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Given odds in favour for three independent critics A, B, C, find the probability that at least 2 critics favour the book (majority in favour).

given_information.to_find: P(majority in favour) = P(at least 2 out of 3 favour)

phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Majority means at least 2 critics favour: cases are (A∩B∩C'), (A∩B'∩C), (A'∩B∩C), and (A∩B∩C). Sum all four since critics are independent.

key_concepts: Odds in favour: a:b means P = a/(a+b)
Mutually exclusive cases for exactly 2 or 3 in favour

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Convert odds to probabilities, find complements, enumerate all cases where at least 2 critics favour (using independence to multiply), and sum the probabilities.
logical_steps: Step 1: Convert odds to probabilities P(A), P(B), P(C)
Step 3: Compute each of the 4 cases

phase_5_verify_answer.verification: 18 + 32 + 60 + 24 = 134. All four cases of at least 2 critics favouring: 18/343 + 32/343 + 60/343 + 24/343 = 134/343 ✓
